lines.text: This is the story of one app. From a no, to a launch, to a binder for everyone you call family.
Some weeks I'm the mom, the daughter, and the one who knows where everything is.
My dad's insurance. The kids' passports. And Sam's car registration, because he's in Lisbon for a year and I'm the one he trusts.
We wanted to build something for her. But first, we had to fail at something else.
Our first app was turned down twice. It wasn't different enough. Apple was right.
So we stopped resubmitting and held on to the one thing that was good.
On the twenty-first of September, we started again.
Before we had one idea, we built the filter that every idea had to pass.
Useful for years. Not something the phone already does. Private by design. Buildable in weeks, not years. And a business from day one.
One idea made it through all five. We started with the hardest version: looking after a parent.
Next, we stopped guessing.
We searched the store like a tired person at eleven at night. We read the one-star reviews. And every form and rule in the app comes from whoever publishes it. States, Medicare, the FTC.
Six building blocks. Everything the app does is one of them, or a mix of them.
For a few days it was called On Behalf. Then we found a better word.
Provisum. Latin for provided for. What you want everyone you love to be.
Then the look. Calm, because people open this app on hard days.
Every screen was checked at the biggest text sizes. When something broke, we redesigned the screen, not the text.
Native Swift, for iPhone, Apple Watch and widgets. Nothing in between.
Everything belongs to a binder, and a binder belongs to a person: your dad, your daughter, yourself, your partner, a friend, even the dog.
Every date from every source joins one list and gets the reminder that fits it. Passports get nine, six and three months. A bill gets the day before.
There is no Veyago server. Your data lives on your phone and in your own iCloud. Sharing goes straight to the people you invite.
The emergency card is encrypted on your iPhone before it goes anywhere.
We carried the engine over from our first app, and rebuilt everything around it.
Seven days after the first sketch, App Review said yes.
We launched in the United States, where Veyago does business, with its states' forms and Medicare built in.
On day one we got the price wrong. On day two we fixed it.
Then we looked at what we'd built, and at who we'd left out.
It was never only my dad.
Version one was a binder for a parent. Nobody looks after just one person.
Sam's car, Dad's medications, the kids' passports. Same place. Same calm.
And the biggest change: no more forms. Provisum asks one question at a time.
Every person gets the documents, dates and packets that fit them. A child's binder isn't a parent's.
Everything we drew.
Built natively. Tested at every text size.
And it's all on my phone. Not on anyone's server.
Provisum. It's Latin for provided for. For everyone you call family.
